entries.2a12b08da9f518b716e0524012b144e717d3fdb2: <div annotateRef="Bible:Matt.5.45" annotateType="commentary" osisID="Matt.5.45" sID="gen97357" type="section"/> <div sID="gen97358" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">45. </hi><hi type="italic">That ye may be the children of your Father who is in heaven.</hi> When he expressly declares, that no man will be a child of God, unless he <hi type="italic">loves those who hate him, </hi>who shall dare to say, that we are not bound to observe this doctrine? The statement amounts to this, “Whoever shall wish to be accounted a Christian, let him <hi type="italic">love his enemies.” </hi>It is truly horrible and monstrous, that the world should have been covered with such thick darkness, for three or four centuries, as not to see that it is an express command, and that every one who neglects it is struck out of the number of the children of God.<div eID="gen97358" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen97359" type="x-p"/>It ought to be observed that, when the example of God is held out for our imitation, this does not imply, that it would be becoming in us to do whatever God does. He frequently punishes the wicked, and drives the wicked out of the world. In this respect, he does not desire us to imitate him: for the judgment of the world, which is his prerogative, does not belong to us. But it is his will, that we should imitate his fatherly goodness and liberality. This was perceived, not only by heathen philosophers, but by some wicked despisers of godliness, who have made this open confession, that in nothing do men resemble God more than in doing good. In short, Christ assures us, that this will be a mark of our adoption, if we are <hi type="italic">kind to the unthankful and evil. </hi>And yet you are not to understand, that our liberality makes us the children of God: but the same Spirit, who is the <hi type="italic">witness, </hi>(<reference osisRef="Bible:Rom.8.16">Romans 8:16</reference>,) <hi type="italic">earnest, </hi>(<reference osisRef="Bible:Eph.1.14">Ephesians 1:14</reference>,) and <hi type="italic">seal, </hi>(<reference osisRef="Bible:Eph.4.30">Ephesians 4:30</reference>,) of our free adoption, corrects the wicked affections of the flesh, which are opposed to charity. Christ therefore proves from the effect, that none are the children of God, but those who resemble him in gentleness and kindness.<div eID="gen97359" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen97360" type="x-p"/>Luke says, <hi type="italic">and you shall be the children of the Highest.</hi> Not that any man acquires this honor for himself, or begins to be a <hi type="italic">child of God, </hi>when he <hi type="italic">loves his enemies; </hi>but because, when it is intended to excite us to do what is right, Scripture frequently employs this manner of speaking, and represents as a reward the free gifts of God. The reason is, he looks at the design of our calling, which is, that, in consequence of the likeness of God having been formed anew in us, we may live a devout and holy life. <hi type="italic">He maketh his sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sendeth rain on the just and the unjust. </hi>He quotes two instances of the divine kindness toward us, which are not only well known to us, but common to all: and this very participation excites us the more powerfully to act in a similar manner towards each other, though, by a <hi type="italic">synecdoche,</hi> <note n="422"> <div sID="gen97361" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="fr">Combien qu'il comprend sous ces deux d'autres infinis tesmoignages, par une figure dont nous avons souvent parle, nommee Synecdoche</foreign>.” — “Though, under these two, he includes innumerable other testimonies, by a figure, of which we have frequently spoken, called <hi type="italic">Synecdoche.”</hi><div eID="gen97361" type="x-p"/> </note> he includes a vast number of other favors.<div eID="gen97360" type="x-p"/> <div annotateRef="Bible:Matt.5.45" annotateType="commentary" eID="gen97357" osisID="Matt.5.45" type="section"/>
entries.141e02e3258568858f94d8cd5b5a3455406640fe: <div annotateRef="Bible:Matt.5.46" annotateType="commentary" osisID="Matt.5.46" sID="gen97362" type="section"/> <div sID="gen97363" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">46. </hi><hi type="italic">Do not even the publicans the same?</hi> In the same sense, Luke calls them <hi type="italic">sinners, </hi>that is, wicked and unprincipled men. Not that the office is condemned in itself; for the <hi type="italic">publicans </hi>were collectors of taxes, and as princes have a right to impose taxes, so it is lawful to levy them from the people. But they are so called, because men of this class are usually covetous and rapacious, nay, deceitful and cruel; and because among the Jews they were the agents of a wicked tyranny. If any one shall conclude from the words of Christ, that <hi type="italic">publicans </hi>are the basest of all men, he will argue ill, for our Lord employs the ordinary phraseology. His meaning is: those who are nearly devoid of humanity have some appearance of discharging mutual duties, when they see it to be for their own advantage.<div eID="gen97363" type="x-p"/> <div annotateRef="Bible:Matt.5.46" annotateType="commentary" eID="gen97362" osisID="Matt.5.46" type="section"/>

48. You shall therefore be perfect. This perfection does not mean equality, but relates solely to resemblance.
“Ceste perfection ne signifie pas qu'il y ait une.equalite et mesme mesure, mais elle se rapporte seulement a quelque ressemblance ou ap-proche.” — “That perfection does not mean that there is an equality or thee same measure, but it relates solely to some resemblance or approach.”
However distant we are from the perfection of God, we are said to be perfect, as he is perfect, when we aim at the same object, which he presents to us in Himself. Should it be thought preferable, we may state it thus. There is no comparison here made between God and us: but the perfection of God means, first, that free and pure kindness, which is not induced by the expectation of gain; — and, secondly, that remarkable goodness, which contends with the malice and ingratitude of men. This appears more clearly from the words of Luke, Be ye therefore merciful, as your Father also is merciful: for mercy is contrasted with a mercenary regard, which is founded on private advantage.
MATTHEW 6: 1-4
Matthew 6:1-4
1. Beware lest ye do your alms before men, that you may be seen by them: otherwise you have not a reward with your Father who is in heaven. 2. Therefore, when thou doest alms, let there not be a sound of trumpets before thee, as hypocrites do in synagogues and in streets, that they may be glorified by men. Verily I say to you, They have their reward. 3. But when thou shalt do alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth: 4. That thy alms may be in secret, and thy Father, who seeth in secret, will reward thee openly.

<ns0:div xmlns:ns0="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5" type="chapter">
               <ns0:head>CHAP. V.</ns0:head>
               <ns0:p n="1">1 ANd seeing the multitudes, he went up in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />to a mountain, and when he was set, his disciples came unto him.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="2">2 And he opened his mouth, and taught them, saying.<ns0:note place="bottom">The last Chapter concluded with telling us, that a great multitude followed Christ, which he observing, that he might with more Conveniency to himself, and Advantage to them, speak what he had to say, he went up into a <ns0:hi>Mountain</ns0:hi>; and sitting down, after the manner of the <ns0:hi>Iewish Doctors</ns0:hi> to shew their Authority, which our Saviour also at other times observed. <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 26.55. <ns0:hi>Luk</ns0:hi> 4.20. <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 8.2. h<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>s Disciples came to him, both those strictly so called, and others also, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> the multitude, mentioned in the la<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t Chapter or some of them, and he began to speak to them, with Freedo<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, so as the multitude might hear, Christ thought it as lawful to Preach in the <ns0:hi>Mountain,</ns0:hi> as in the <ns0:hi>Synagogues</ns0:hi>: Nor did his Disciples, doubt the <ns0:hi>Lawfulness of hearing them,</ns0:hi> where ever he thought fit to speak.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="3">3 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luk. 6.20.</ns0:note> Blessed <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> the poor in spirit for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.<ns0:note place="bottom">Happy are they, who tho they be not Rich in this Worlds goods, yet have a Spirit suted to their State and Condition, not looking for their Consolation here, but having a Poor, and low Opinion of the World, and all that is therein, looking af<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter more excellent Riches, and in order to it, are of broken and <ns0:hi>Contrite Spirits,</ns0:hi> for their manifold sins, and cannot entertain any Proud Opinion of their own Righteousness, but fly unto the free Grace of God, and the Righteousness of the Lord Jesus Christ. Not the Great, and Rich, and Proud Men of the World are happy, but these are the Blessed Men, for true H<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>p<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />piness lyeth not in Worldly Po<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>se<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>sions<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> but in the Favour of God, and a right to the Kingdom of Heaven, and that these Men have, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 34.18. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 51.17. <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 66.2.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="4">4. <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Isa. 61.3. Luk. 6.21.</ns0:note> Blessed <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> they that mourn, for they shall be comforted.<ns0:note place="bottom">The World is mistaken in accounting<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> the jocund, and merry Companions the only happy Men, their mirth is Madness, and their joy will be like crakling of Thorns under a Pot, but those are rather the happy Men who mourn, yea such are most certainly Happy, who mourn out of Duty in the Sense of their own sins, or of the sins of others, or who mourn out of choice rather to suffer Afflictions, and Persecutions with the People of God, than to injoy the Pleasure of sin for a Season. Tho such sufferings do excite in them natural Pa<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>sions, yet it is a Blessed mourning, for those are the blessed Te<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>rs which God will wipe at last from Peoples Eyes, and such are these, <ns0:hi>They shall be Comforted</ns0:hi> either in this Life, with the Consola<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tions of the Spirit, or with their <ns0:hi>Masters joy</ns0:hi> in the Life that is to come, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 61.3. <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 16.20. <ns0:hi>Iames</ns0:hi> 1.12. So as this <ns0:hi>Promise,</ns0:hi> and Declaration of Blessedness<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> is not to be extended to all Mourners, but only to such as God hath made so, or who in Duty have made themselves so, obeying some Com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mand of God; for Sympathizing with Go<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>s Glory, or with his afflicted People<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 
                     <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 12.15. or Te<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>tifying their Repen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tance for their sins, for there is a mourning, which is a meer na<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tural effect of Passion, and a <ns0:hi>Worldly sorrow which worketh unto Death,</ns0:hi> as well as a <ns0:hi>Godly sorrow, working Repentance to Salvation,</ns0:hi> 2<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 
                     <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 7.10.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="5">5 Blessed <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 37.11.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> the meek, for they shall inherit the earth.<ns0:note place="bottom">Men count the <ns0:hi>Hectors</ns0:hi> of the World happy, whom none can provoke, but they must expect as good as they bring, <ns0:hi>an Eye for an Eye, and a Tooth for a Tooth</ns0:hi>: But I tell you these are not truly Happy, they are tortured with their own Passi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ons, as their hand is against every one, so every Mans hand is against them, besides that there is a God, who will revenge the wrongs they do But the <ns0:hi>meek</ns0:hi> who can be angry, but re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />strain their wrath in Obedience to the Will of God, and will not be angry, unless they can be angry and not sin: Nor will easily be provoked by others, but rather use <ns0:hi>soft words to pacifie wrath,</ns0:hi> and give place to the Passions, of others these are the <ns0:hi>Blessed Men</ns0:hi>; for tho others may by their Sword, and their Bow, conquer a great deal of Earth to their Will, and Power: Yet they will never quietly and comfortably inherit, or possess it, they are <ns0:hi>Possessors malae fidei,</ns0:hi> forcible Posse<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>sors, and they will injoy what they have, as rapacious Birds injoy their's unquietly, every one hath his Gun ready Charged, and Cockt against them: But those who are of meek and quiet Spirits, tho they may not take so deep Root in the Earth, as others more bouterous, yet there will be no Worm at the Root of what they have, and they shall enjoy what God gi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />veth them with more quiet, and certainty, and God will pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vide for them, <ns0:hi>Verily they shall be fed, Psal.</ns0:hi> 37.3.11.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="6">6 Blessed <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> they which do hunger, and thirst after righteousness, for they shall be filled.<ns0:note place="bottom">You see many Men and Women, <ns0:hi>Hungring,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Thirsting</ns0:hi> after sensual Satisfactions, or after <ns0:hi>sensible Injoyments;</ns0:hi> these are unhappy miserable Men, they often <ns0:hi>Hunger, and Thirst,</ns0:hi> and are not <ns0:hi>satisfied</ns0:hi>: But I will shew you a more excellent way, a more excellent Object of your <ns0:hi>Hunger</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Thirst,</ns0:hi> that is a <ns0:hi>Righteousness,</ns0:hi> both a <ns0:hi>Righteousness</ns0:hi> wherein you may stand before God, which is in me, <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 23.6. and is revealed <ns0:hi>from Faith to Faith, Rom.</ns0:hi> 1.17. and the <ns0:hi>Righteousness</ns0:hi> of an Holy Life. Those are Blessed Men, who <ns0:hi>first seek the Kingdom of Heaven, and the Righteousness</ns0:hi> thereof, God will fill these Men with what they desire, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 55.1, 2. <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 1.53. There are some who understand this Text, of an <ns0:hi>Hun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gring</ns0:hi> after the clearing of their Innocency towards Men<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> which is natural to just and innocent Persons falsly accused, and tra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />duced, and they have a Promise of being filled, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 37.6. but I see no reason to conclude this, the Sense of this Text.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:225" />7 Blessed <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> the merciful, for they shall ob<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tain mercy.<ns0:note place="bottom">The Men of the World bless themselves, if they can take Care of themselves, let others do what they will, and as well as they can: But I tell you, that those alone are the Blessed Men, who are touched with a true Sense and feeling of the Wants and Miseries of others, and that not out of a meer Goodness, and Tenderness of Nature, but out of a true Obe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dience to the Will of God, and a Sense of his Love to them, and Faith in his Promises, and moved from these Principles, do not only Pity, and Compassionate them, and wish them well, but extend their helping hand to them, sutably to their Miseries: For these Men shall obtain mercy, and that not only from Men, if they come into Straits and Distress, but from the hand of God. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 37.26. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 112.5. he doth not say they shall merit Mercy at Gods hand, but they shall be <ns0:hi>Mercified,</ns0:hi> they shall <ns0:hi>obtain Mercy.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 Blessed <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> the <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 24.4.</ns0:note> pure in heart, for they shall see God.<ns0:note place="bottom">The Men of the World bless those who appear Pure, and Holy to men, and put on a Vizard, and Mask of Purity: Tho they be but painted Sepulchers<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and their Hearts be as Cages of all unclean Birds: But those alone are Blessed, who being washed from their filthiness by my Blood, are of a <ns0:hi>sincere</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>upright</ns0:hi> Heart, tho they be not legally Pure, and free from all sin; yet are so Pure as that God will accept them, the bent of their Hearts being after Holiness. Who have not an Heart, and an Heart, no doubleness of mind, who are Per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sons in whom is no Guile. For tho no mortal Eye can see, and comprehend the Essence of God, yet these Men shall by an Eye of Faith, <ns0:hi>see</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>enjoy God</ns0:hi> in this Life, tho in a Glass more darkly, and <ns0:hi>in the Life to come, Face to Face,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>as he is,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 13.12. <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 12.14. 1 <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 3.2.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 Blessed <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> the peace-makers, for they shall be called the children of God.<ns0:note place="bottom">The World blesseth the boisterous unquiet Party of it, that can never be still, but are continually thinking of more Worlds to Conquer, and blowing up the Coals of <ns0:hi>War, Division,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Sedition.</ns0:hi> But they are Blessed indeed, who study to be quiet, seeking Peace, and pursuing it; and are so far from sowing the Seeds of Discord or blowing those Coals, that their great study is to make Peace between God, and Man, and betwixt a Man, and his Neighbour, doing this in Obedi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ence to God, and out of a Principle of Love to God, and Men: For those that do so, shall approve themselves <ns0:hi>like un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />to God</ns0:hi> to be his Children, and so they shall be called. To be <ns0:hi>called,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>to be</ns0:hi> is much the same, so what <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> said, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 21.12. is interpreted by <ns0:hi>Paul, Rom.</ns0:hi> 9.7.8. So what is said by <ns0:hi>Matthew, Matth.</ns0:hi> 21.12. is interpreted, by <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 19.46. what was said by St. <ns0:hi>Iohn, Chap.</ns0:hi> 1.13. is interpreted, 1 <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 3.1. for God is the God of Peace, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 14.33.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 Blessed <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> they who are persecuted for righteousness sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.<ns0:note place="bottom">The Men of the World judge those Men very unhappy and miserable, whom their Rulers make the Objects of their <ns0:hi>Wrath</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Malice,</ns0:hi> and pursue violently to the loss of their <ns0:hi>Estates, Liberties,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Lives</ns0:hi> never considering the Cause, for which they are so pursued: But they are quite mistaken. For that Man who is pursued by such <ns0:hi>Violence,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>hunted</ns0:hi> up<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on this Account, because to please Men, he durst not sin against God, but Labours to keep a <ns0:hi>Conscience void of offence, both toward God, and toward Men, Acts</ns0:hi> 24.16 is a <ns0:hi>Blessed Man,</ns0:hi> and if he be hunted out of the Kingdoms of the Earth, yet he shall be hunted but to Heaven, for to such Men be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />longeth the Kingdom of God in Glory, <ns0:hi>Iames</ns0:hi> 1.12. 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 3.14. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 4.13.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 Blessed are ye when men shall revile you, and persecute <ns0:hi>ye,</ns0:hi>
                  <ns0:note place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>lying for my names sake.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> and shall say all manner of evil against you falsly for my sake.<ns0:note place="bottom">Revising, and speaking Evil of Personss falsly, because of their Profession of Christ, and because they dare not sin a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gainst God, is a species of Persecution. <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 21.9. <ns0:hi>Gal.</ns0:hi> 4.29. tho the lowest Degree of it. It hath been the constant lot of Gods Servants, <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> said, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 35.11. that <ns0:hi>false Witnesses</ns0:hi> did <ns0:hi>rise up,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>laid to his Charge things that he knew not.</ns0:hi> Thus <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Christ</ns0:hi> were served, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 11.19. <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 7.34. nor is it to be wondred, that those whose Consciences are so <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>eared, that they cannot feel the Guilt of Persecuting o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thers for <ns0:hi>Righteousness sake,</ns0:hi> should not feel the Guilt of <ns0:hi>Ly<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>fa<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>se Swearing.</ns0:hi> But saith our Saviour, you are <ns0:hi>B<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>essed</ns0:hi> when these things happen unto you, 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 4.13.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 Rejoyce, and be exceeding glad, for great <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> your reward in heaven, for so persecuted they the prophets which were before you.<ns0:note place="bottom">Be so far from being troubled, as to count it all <ns0:hi>Ioy,</ns0:hi> when you fall into these Tryals, <ns0:hi>Iames</ns0:hi> 1.2. Let it be Musick in your Ears, to hear that the <ns0:hi>Drunkards</ns0:hi> make you their Song. Rejoyce in your Hearts, express it in your Lips, and Behaviour, <ns0:hi>for great is your reward,</ns0:hi> not of Debt but of Grace, <ns0:hi>for our light and mo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment Afflictions are not worthy to be compared with an E<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ternal and exceeding weight of Glory,</ns0:hi> where there is no Propor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion, there can be no Merit: Especially, when <ns0:hi>it is given to us on the behalf of Christ</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>suffer, Phil.</ns0:hi> 1.29. <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> upon this Argument saith, 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 4.14. <ns0:hi>The Spirit of God and of Glory resteth upon us.</ns0:hi> Our Saviour adds: <ns0:hi>For so they per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />secuted the Prophets before you.</ns0:hi> The Magistrates, and the <ns0:hi>Rulers</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> persecuted <ns0:hi>Elijah, Micaiah, Ieremiah, Amos</ns0:hi> and the rest of the Prophets whom you succeed, not in time only, but in the same Office of revealing the mind of God to the People.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 Ye are the salt of the earth, But if the salt hath lost its savour, wherewith shall it be sal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ted? It is thence forth good for nothing but to be cast out, and to be troden under foot of men.<ns0:note place="bottom">In our Christian Course we are not to trouble our selves with what Men say of us, and do unto us, but only to at<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tend to our Duty of Holiness, and <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> Exemplary Life, which is what our Saviour presseth plainly, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 16. and leads his Hearers to it by four Comparisons, which he instituteth be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />twixt them and four other things, the first we have in this Verse, <ns0:hi>ye are the Salt of the Earth.</ns0:hi> The Doctrine which you profess is so, a thing as opposite as can be to the Putrefaction of the World, both in respect to corrupt Doctrine, and cor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rupt Manners (therefore by the way it will be no wonder, if they resist it by Reviling and Persecuting you) you are the <ns0:hi>Salt of the Earth,</ns0:hi> through the Grace of God bestowed up<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on you, <ns0:hi>Mar.</ns0:hi> 9.50. <ns0:hi>Col.</ns0:hi> 4.6. If it were not for the num<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ber of sound and painful Ministers, and Holy and Gracious Persons, the Earth, would be but a stinking Dunghil of Drunkards, unclean Persons, Theeves, Murderers, unrighteous Persons, that would be a stench in the Nostrils of a Pure and Holy God. Look as it is in the World, if the <ns0:hi>Salt</ns0:hi> hath lost its <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>avour, its Acrimony by which it opposeth Putrefaction in Fish, and Flesh, not the Fish or Flesh only will be good for nothing, but the <ns0:hi>Salt</ns0:hi> it self so <ns0:hi>infatuated</ns0:hi> (as it is in the <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi>) will be good for nothing, but to be <ns0:hi>cast upon a Dunghil and trodden under Foot.</ns0:hi> So it is with Ministers of the Gospel, so with the Professors of it, if they <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 span">
                        <ns0:desc>〈…〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> their soundness in the Faith, and Holiness of Life, they <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> no value, nay they are worse than other men. Mony <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> clipt in pieces, and hath lost its usefulness as Coyn, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 span">
                        <ns0:desc>〈…〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> use for a Gold-Smith, Meat corrupted, if it will not <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> Men, yet will feed <ns0:hi>Dogs, Salt</ns0:hi> is good for nothin<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> more are pretended Ministers or Christians, their <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 span">
                        <ns0:desc>〈…〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> lyes in their savour, if that be lost, wherewith shall <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 span">
                        <ns0:desc>〈…〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> salted: Of what use are they, unless to cause the Name of God and Religion to be blasphemed. Such another similitude the prophet useth, <ns0:hi>Ezeck.</ns0:hi> 15.2.3.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 Ye are the light of the world, A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid.<ns0:note place="bottom">You that are to be my Apostles, are so <ns0:hi>Eminently,</ns0:hi> but all you that are my Disciples are so also. <ns0:hi>Christ is the Light of the World, Ioh.</ns0:hi> 1.5.9. but tho the Sun be the Light of the World, yet it doth not follow, that the <ns0:hi>Moon</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Stars</ns0:hi> also are not so, he is the <ns0:hi>Original</ns0:hi> Light, the great <ns0:hi>Light</ns0:hi> who hath Light from and in himself. The Ministers of the Gospel are the <ns0:hi>Lights of the</ns0:hi> World also, the Angels of Churches are <ns0:hi>Stars, Rev.</ns0:hi> 1.20. and Holy Persons are <ns0:hi>Children of the Light,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Thess.</ns0:hi> 5.5. <ns0:hi>A City that is set upon an Hill cannot be hid.</ns0:hi> The Church is often called the <ns0:hi>City of God</ns0:hi> Christ compares his People here not to a <ns0:hi>City,</ns0:hi> but to a City upon a Hill, so that all which our Saviour mentions a <ns0:hi>City</ns0:hi> here for, is the Conspicuity of a City so built. It is as much as if our Saviour should have said: You had need be Holy for your Conversation cannot be hid, any more than a City can that is builded upon an Hill, which is obvious to every Eye. All Mens Eyes will be upon you.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 Neither do men light a candle, and put it under a <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Mar. 4.11. Luk. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 11.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> bushel, but upon a candlestick, and it giveth light unto all that are in the house.<ns0:note place="bottom">You ought also to consider the End, why I have Communi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cated of my Light unto you, it is in part the same with that of Men, when they light up a Candle in a Room, which is to shew Light to all those that are in the Room, they do not use to light it up to hide it under a Vessel, or a Bushel: So I have not Communicated my Truths, or my Grace unto you meerly for your own use, but for others use. It is said of <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> (by our Saviour) he was a <ns0:hi>burning and shining Light</ns0:hi>: So is every true Minister of the Gospel, yea and every true Christian; not only a <ns0:hi>burning Light,</ns0:hi> burning with Love to God, and Zeal for God, and Love to, and Zeal for the Souls of others: But also a <ns0:hi>shining Light,</ns0:hi> Communicating his Light to o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thers, both by <ns0:hi>Instruction,</ns0:hi> and an <ns0:hi>Holy Conversation.</ns0:hi> Others pretended Candles were never of Gods lighting.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 Let your light so shine before men, that
<ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:225" />
they may <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Pet 2.12.</ns0:note> see your good works, and glorifie your Father which is in heaven.<ns0:note place="bottom">Our Sav<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>our now plainly tells us, what he intended by the Comp<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>risons before mentioned. Let the <ns0:hi>Lig<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>t</ns0:hi> of that Do<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ctrine which you receive from me, and the <ns0:hi>Light</ns0:hi> of your Ho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly Conversation (the latter by the following words, seemeth to be here Principally intended) so <ns0:hi>shine before Men,</ns0:hi> be so Evident<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and apparent unto Men: <ns0:hi>That they may</ns0:hi> see your <ns0:hi>Good works,</ns0:hi> all sorts of Good works, whatsoever I have Com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />manded<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> or shall Command you, and as I Command you, and in Obedience to such Commands, otherwise they are no Good works, <ns0:hi>and Glorifie your Father which is in the Heavens.</ns0:hi> You are not in your good Actions to aim at your selves, to be seen of Men, as <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 6.1. nor meerly at doing good to others, the <ns0:hi>Good works, Tit.</ns0:hi> 3.14. are <ns0:hi>to be maintained for necessary uses,</ns0:hi> but having a Primary and Principal respect to the <ns0:hi>Glorifying of your Father,</ns0:hi> for <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 15.8. <ns0:hi>herein is my Father Glorified, if you bear much Fruit</ns0:hi>: Not that we can add any thing to Gods essential Glory, but we may predi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cate and manifest his Glory. Which now we can do by <ns0:hi>Good works,</ns0:hi> if they proceed from <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 span">
                        <ns0:desc>〈…〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, and <ns0:hi>Liberty</ns0:hi> of our own <ns0:hi>Wills,</ns0:hi> not from his <ns0:hi>special Efficacious Grace,</ns0:hi> is hard to understand. Our Father is said to be in the Heavens, be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause tho his Essential Presence filleth all places, yet he is pleased there more than any where to manifest his <ns0:hi>Glory</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Majesty.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 Think not that I am come to destroy the Law or the Prophets, I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.<ns0:note place="bottom">There are so many Adversaries, <ns0:hi>Iews, Papists, Socinians, Anabaptists, Antinomians,</ns0:hi> &c. That make their advanta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ges of this Text, for the Establishing their several Errors, that it would require a Volume to vindicate it from their several Exceptions, those who desire Satisfaction may read <ns0:hi>Spanhe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mis Dub. Evang.</ns0:hi> 12.3. The plain Sense of the Text is this: It would have been a great Cavil with the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> especially (who had a great reverence for the Law) if either our Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />viours Enemies amongst them, could have perswaded People, that Christ came to destroy the Law and the Prophets: Or his own hearers had entertained from his Discourse any such Apprehensions. Our Saviour designing in his following Dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />course, to give a more full and strict Interpretation of the Law than had been given by the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> and other Jewish Doctors, prefaceth that Discourse, with a Protestation against his coming to <ns0:hi>destroy the Law,</ns0:hi> and averring that he came to fulfil it. It is manifest by his following Discourse, that he Principally spake of the <ns0:hi>Moral Law,</ns0:hi> tho he also fulfilled the <ns0:hi>Ceremonial Law,</ns0:hi> he being the <ns0:hi>Antitype</ns0:hi> in whom all the <ns0:hi>Types</ns0:hi> of that had their Complement, and real fulfilling and Ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />complishment. Saith he, I am not come to <ns0:hi>Destroy,</ns0:hi> and put an end to the <ns0:hi>Moral Law.</ns0:hi> I am come to fulfil it, not to <ns0:hi>fill it up,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Papists and Socinians</ns0:hi> contend, adding any new Precept to it, but by yielding my self a Personal obedience to it, by giving a fuller and stricter Interpretation of it, than you have formerly had, and by taking the Curse of it (so far as concerneth my Disciples) upon my self, and giving a just Satisfaction to Divine Justice for it. The greatest Objection urged against Christ destroying part of the Law, and adding new Precepts to the Moral Law, is that about the <ns0:hi>Change of the Sabbath,</ns0:hi> but this is none, if we consider, that the <ns0:hi>Moral Law</ns0:hi> required no more than <ns0:hi>one Day of seven</ns0:hi> to be kept as a Day <ns0:hi>of Holy Rest,</ns0:hi> not this or that particular Day, for the particular Day, the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> learned it from the <ns0:hi>Ceremonial Law,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Christians</ns0:hi> learn theirs from Christ's, and the <ns0:hi>Apostles Pra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ctice.</ns0:hi> Nor is it any Objection against this, that the seventh Day from the <ns0:hi>Creation</ns0:hi> is mentioned in the Law, to those who know how to distinguish betwixt the <ns0:hi>Precept</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Argu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment,</ns0:hi> the seventh from the <ns0:hi>Creation</ns0:hi> is not in the <ns0:hi>Precept,</ns0:hi> but in the <ns0:hi>Argument. For in six Days, &c.</ns0:hi> Now there is nothing more ordinary than to have Arguments of a particu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lar Temporary Concernment used to inforce Precepts of an eternal Obligation, where the Precepts were first given to that particular People, as to whom those Arguments were of Force, an instance of which is in the first Commandment, as well as in this: As on the other side Arguments of universal Force, are oft annexed to Precepts, which had but a particular Obligation, upon a particular People for a time. Thus in the Ceremonial Law, we often find it is an Argument to inforce many Ceremonial Precepts. <ns0:hi>For I am the Lord thy God.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 For verily I say unto you, till Heaven and Earth pass, <ns0:note place="margin">Luk. 16.17.</ns0:note> one jot, or one title shall in no wise pass from the Law, till all be fulfilled.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Amen I say unto you,</ns0:hi> so it is in the <ns0:hi>Greek,</ns0:hi> a Phrase as some observe never used, but by God and Christ himself who is the <ns0:hi>Amen,</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Faithful and true Witness, Rev.</ns0:hi> 3.14. tho the Servants of God have sometimes used it, as an Ad<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />verb of wishing. It is by most concluded a <ns0:hi>form of an Oath,</ns0:hi> God by it Swearing by his Truth and Faithfulness [<ns0:hi>till Heaven, and Earth,</ns0:hi> &c.] that is the Law is the certain and unchangeable Will of God concerning reasonable Creatures, and it shall never be altered in the least Title, nor ever be abolishe<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, you may therefore be secure that I come into the World upon no such Errand.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">James 2.10.</ns0:note> Whosoever theref ore shall break one of these least Commandements, and shall teach men so, he shall be called the least in the Kingdom of Heaven; but whosoever shall do, and teach <ns0:hi>them</ns0:hi> shall be called great in the Kingdom of Heaven.<ns0:note place="bottom">Whosoever shall in his Practice violate but one of the Commandements of God, which the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> judge of the <ns0:hi>least,</ns0:hi> and which possibly are so, compared with others, and shall teach Men that they may do, as he doth; making suc<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> false Intepretations of the Law, as may warrant such a Pra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ctice, he shall be accounted, of the least value, and Esteem in the Church of God, and shall never come in the Kingdom of Glory: But he who shall strictly and uniformly obey all the Commandements and teach others to do the like, by his Doctrine and Example, that Man shall have a great Renown, and Reputation in the Church which is the Kingdom of Hea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven upon Earth, and shall have a great reward in the Kingdom of Glory hereafter.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 For I say unto you, that except your righ<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />teousness <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luk. 11.39.</ns0:note> shall exceed <ns0:hi>the righteousness</ns0:hi> of the Scribes and Pharisees ye shall in no case enter into the Kingdom of Heaven.<ns0:note place="bottom">I am so far from giving a Liberty to the Violation of my Fathers Law, (as the <ns0:hi>Scribes and Pharisees</ns0:hi> may possibly sug<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gest) that I assure you, that unless your <ns0:hi>Obedience to it</ns0:hi> ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceed that Obedience, which the <ns0:hi>Scribes and Pharisees</ns0:hi> teach you, and themselves Practise, <ns0:hi>you shall never come in Heaven.</ns0:hi> What the Righteousness of the <ns0:hi>Scribes</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> was, we cannot better learn than from St. <ns0:hi>Paul,</ns0:hi> who was himself a <ns0:hi>Pharisee,</ns0:hi> and bred up at the Feet of <ns0:hi>Gamaliel</ns0:hi> a great Doctor amongst them, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 23.5. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 26.5. <ns0:hi>Phil.</ns0:hi> 3.5. That it was a <ns0:hi>Righteousness of works</ns0:hi> appeareth from <ns0:hi>Phil.</ns0:hi> 3. and the whole Epistles to the <ns0:hi>Romans,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Galathians,</ns0:hi> and their not owning Christ as the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi>: Nor <ns0:hi>believing</ns0:hi> on him, <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 7.48. made it impossible that it should be any other, that they lookt upon their meer Obedience to the <ns0:hi>Ceremonial Law</ns0:hi> as their Righteousness, cannot be proved, yea the contrary is enough Evident, by their Obedience to the <ns0:hi>Moral Law,</ns0:hi> ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cording to the Interpretation they put upon it. But their In<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />terpretation of the Moral Law was so short and jejune, that it is manifest that their <ns0:hi>Righteousness,</ns0:hi> was not only a Righte<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ousness <ns0:hi>not of Faith,</ns0:hi> but <ns0:hi>of Works,</ns0:hi> but <ns0:hi>Works</ns0:hi> that were very <ns0:hi>imperfect</ns0:hi> and short of what the true Sense of the Law required, our Saviour afterward proveth. That is to say, it was <ns0:hi>no Righ<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />teousness,</ns0:hi> for <ns0:hi>he that keepeth</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>whole Law, if he be Guilty</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>one Point is Guilty of all, Ia.</ns0:hi> 2.10.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 Ye have heard that it was said by them of old time, thou <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ex. 20.13. Deut. 5.17.</ns0:note> shalt not kill, and whosoever shall kill, shall be in danger of the Judgment.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 But I say unto you, That whosoever is angry with his Brother without a cause, shall be in danger of the Judgment, and whosoever shall say unto his Brother, Raca, shall be in danger of the Councel, but whosoever shall say, Thou fool, shall be in danger of hell fire.<ns0:note place="bottom">The <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> in their Lectures upon the Law usually thus prefaced, <ns0:hi>It was said to them of old time,</ns0:hi> this saith Christ, you have heard, <ns0:hi>Thou shalt not kill</ns0:hi>: This was spoken by God in Mount <ns0:hi>Sinai,</ns0:hi> it was the sixth of the ten words then spoke, and <ns0:hi>whosoever shall Kill, shall be in danger of the Iudgment</ns0:hi>: This now was the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> addition, for we read of no such addition to the Law, as deliverd, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 20.13. Thus they mixed their Traditions with the word of God, which po<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>sible might be the reason of their saying rather, <ns0:hi>It was said to them of old time,</ns0:hi> than <ns0:hi>it was said by Moses:</ns0:hi> Or, <ns0:hi>It was said in the Law of God,</ns0:hi> for under that Phrase, <ns0:hi>It was said to the Ancients,</ns0:hi> they both comprehended the Law given by <ns0:hi>Moses,</ns0:hi> to the Ancient People of God, and also their own Traditions, and false Glosses, which tho not so Ancient as the Law, yet had obtained for some considerable time, in the corrupt State of the <ns0:hi>Iews: Shall be Guilty of,</ns0:hi>or <ns0:hi>Obnoxious unto the Iudgment,</ns0:hi> not to the Wrath and Vengeance of God, of that they said nothing, but to those Courts of Judgment which sate amongst them, to administer Justice in criminal Causes. As if this Law of God had been only intended to uphold Peace, and to preserve humane Society, and Civil order. <ns0:hi>Thou shalt not Kill</ns0:hi> (that is, as they interpreted) thou shalt not with<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />out a Warrant from God, or from the Law, actually take a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />way the Life of another. It appears by what followeth, that they extended not this Law, to unjustifiable <ns0:hi>Passions</ns0:hi> in the <ns0:hi>Heart,</ns0:hi> such as <ns0:hi>rash Anger, Malice, revengeful Thoughts</ns0:hi>: Nor to any <ns0:hi>opprobrious</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>revengeful Words.</ns0:hi> But <ns0:hi>I say unto you:</ns0:hi> I shall give you another Sense of this Law. The killing here forbidden is as well, <ns0:hi>Rash and causeless Anger,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>op<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />probrious Threatning Speeches,</ns0:hi> as bloody Actions. <ns0:hi>Whoso<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ever is Angry with his Brother without a cause, shall be in Danger of the Iudgment,</ns0:hi> &c. Our Saviour (as most Inter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />preters judge) speaks this with Allusion to the three Courts amo<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>g<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi>: The one was the <ns0:hi>Court of three Men,</ns0:hi> which only judged of smaller and lighter Causes, not in <ns0:hi>Ca<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pital Causes.</ns0:hi> Another was their <ns0:hi>Court of twenty three Men,</ns0:hi> which much answered our Courts at <ns0:hi>Westminster.</ns0:hi> The third was their <ns0:hi>San<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>edrim</ns0:hi> consisting of seventy Men, which answered our <ns0:hi>Parliament.</ns0:hi> Some think that by <ns0:hi>the Iudgment,</ns0:hi> is meant the first or second of the Courts. By the <ns0:hi>Councel,</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Supe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />riour Courts</ns0:hi> amongst the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> but the Judgment of our <ns0:hi>Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />verend Dr. Light-foot,</ns0:hi> seemeth much more probable, that by the <ns0:hi>Iudgment</ns0:hi> is meant the <ns0:hi>Iudgment</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>God.</ns0:hi> By the <ns0:hi>Coun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cel</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Hell-fire,</ns0:hi> not only the <ns0:hi>Iudgment,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Vengeance of God,</ns0:hi> but the <ns0:hi>Iudgments</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Punishments,</ns0:hi> that are inflicted in the Courts of Men, that are Magistrates, and bear not the Sword in vain; so as the Sense is this. I say unto you, that if a Man doth but in his Heart nourish <ns0:hi>Wrath,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Anger</ns0:hi> a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gainst another, without a <ns0:hi>just Cause,</ns0:hi> and lets it grow up into <ns0:hi>Malice,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Thoughts, and Desires of private Revenge,</ns0:hi> tho he be not by it obnoxious to Courts of Justice, who can only determine upon overt Acts, yet he is accountable to God, and liable to his Judgment, but if Men suffer their <ns0:hi>Passions</ns0:hi> to break out into Reviling terms, and Language, such as <ns0:hi>Raca</ns0:hi> (signifying a Vain Person) or <ns0:hi>thou Fool</ns0:hi> (speaking this from <ns0:hi>Anger</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Malice</ns0:hi>) they are not only liable to the Eternal Vengeance of God, compared to the Fire of <ns0:hi>Gehenna,</ns0:hi> but ought to be subjected to the Punishment of the <ns0:hi>Civil Ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gistrate.</ns0:hi> Every civil Government being by the Law of God, in Order to the prevention of Quarrels, or Blood-shed (which often followeth Revilings each of other) obliged to punish such offences, as being the beginnings of <ns0:hi>Murder, Provocati<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ons</ns0:hi> to it, and <ns0:hi>Indications</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>murderous Hearts,</ns0:hi> Hearts full of that, which in the Eye of God is Murder.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:226" />23 Therefore if thou bring thy Gift to the altar, and there remembrest that thy Brother hath ought against thee.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 Leave there thy Gift before the altar, and go thy way, first be reconciled to thy brother, and then come and offer thy Gift.<ns0:note place="bottom">The <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> were to offer <ns0:hi>Gifts,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Sacrifices, Heb.</ns0:hi> 5.1. Their Gifts were their <ns0:hi>Free-Will-Offerings,</ns0:hi> they were the most <ns0:hi>frequent Oblations</ns0:hi> amongst the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> as may appear from <ns0:hi>Leviticus,</ns0:hi> and what the <ns0:hi>Priests</ns0:hi> pressed with the greatest <ns0:hi>Importunity,</ns0:hi> as may appear from <ns0:hi>Mar.</ns0:hi> 7.11. therefore our Saviour instanceth in these, rather than in other parts of their Worship. Bring unto God the best and most acceptable Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />crifices (in your or the Teachers judgment) that you can, if there be found <ns0:hi>Malice,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>rash Anger</ns0:hi> in your Hearts, God will not accept them. Therefore, how near soever you be come to a Religious Action, if you there remember, that your <ns0:hi>Brother</ns0:hi> hath a just reason to be offended with you<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> for any <ns0:hi>Malice</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>rash Anger,</ns0:hi> shewed, or expressed by you, do not think this will discharge of your Obligation to pay your Homage to God, but forbear a while, <ns0:hi>leave your Gift before the Altar,</ns0:hi> and do what in you lyes to be reconciled to your Brother, to have a placable Spirit to him, to purge your Heart of <ns0:hi>Wrath,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Malice,</ns0:hi> and any Desire of Revenge, and then come and offer <ns0:hi>your Gifts,</ns0:hi> pay that Homage which you owe, and it was in your Heart to pay to God. It is a Text usually applyed with reference to <ns0:hi>Communion</ns0:hi> with God in the <ns0:hi>Lords Supper,</ns0:hi> but equally <ns0:hi>Extensive</ns0:hi> to any other part of Worship, <ns0:hi>hearing the word, Iam.</ns0:hi> 1.21. and <ns0:hi>Prayer,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 2. God accepteth no Service, no Homage from an implacable, Malicious Heart.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">25 Agree with thine Adversary quickly, whilest thou art in the way with him, lest at any time the adversary deliver thee <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luk. 12.58.</ns0:note> to the judge, and the judge deliver thee to the officer, and thou be cast into prison.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">26 Verily I say unto thee, Thou shalt by no means come out thence, until thou hast paid the uttermost farthing.<ns0:note place="bottom">Forasmuch, as the overt Acts, and Expressions of injust Wrath and Malice, are iniquities, punishable by the Judge, let it be the Care of those that will be my Disciples, if by their Passions they have provoked any, and made him their Adver<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sary quickly to agree with them, for you know the ordinary Course of enraged Adversaries amongst Men, is to bring their Actions, and to bring Men before the Civil Judge, and when the Judge upon inquiry hath found them Guilty, he useth to deliver them to the <ns0:hi>Goaler</ns0:hi> to be carried to Prison, until they have fully paid their <ns0:hi>Fines</ns0:hi> for such offences: And forasmuch, as not only the overt Acts, but the Passions which cause such Acts are culpable before God, and make Men obnoxious to his righteous Judgment, and God by them is made, an Adversary to the Soul; as having violated his great Command: <ns0:hi>Thou shalt do no Murther.</ns0:hi> Let all my Disciples, who have been, or may be overtaken with such Faults, by <ns0:hi>Repentance</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Faith in me,</ns0:hi> make their Peace with God in this Life, lest dying in im<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />penitency they be put under the Eternal Displeasure and Wrath of God, from whence they shall never be delivered, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 6.15. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 18.35.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="27">27 Ye have heard, that it was said by them of old time, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Exod <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> Deut. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 28.</ns0:note> Thou shalt not commit adultery.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">28 But I say unto you, That whosoever looketh upon a woman to lust after her, hath committed adultery with her already in his Heart.<ns0:note place="bottom">The <ns0:hi>Scope</ns0:hi> of our <ns0:hi>Saviour</ns0:hi> in these Verses, is the very same as in the Verses immediately preceding, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> to Correct the jejune Interpretation which the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> had put upon the Di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vine Law, and to shew that he instead of coming to destroy the Law, came to <ns0:hi>fulfil it,</ns0:hi> as other ways so by giving a more strict, and true Interpretation of it; and whereas they inter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />preted it, only as to <ns0:hi>Overt Acts,</ns0:hi> which disturb humane Socie<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ty, and break Civil Order, he sheweth that it reacheth to the inward Thoughts, and unlawful Desires of the Heart, and any means that have a Tendenc<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>o such prohibited Acts. It was said by God to those Fathe<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> of the <ns0:hi>Iews, Thou shalt not com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mit Adultery, Exod.</ns0:hi> 20.14. This Law (saith our Saviour) your <ns0:hi>Doctors</ns0:hi> expound, You shall not carnally lye with a Wo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />man that is not your Wife, but there is a great deal more in it than so, for he that but secretly in his Heart desireth such a thing, or taketh Pleasure in such Thoughts, and casts his Eyes upon a Woman, in order to such a thing, is in the sight of God an <ns0:hi>Adul<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />terer.</ns0:hi> Hence we read of <ns0:hi>Eyes full</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Adultery,</ns0:hi> to avoid which, <ns0:hi>Iob</ns0:hi> made a <ns0:hi>Covenant with his Eyes, Iob</ns0:hi> 31.1. and would not, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 7. <ns0:hi>Suffer his Heart to walk after his Eyes</ns0:hi>: We must so in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />terpret the Commandements of God, as not to extend them only to forbid, or command those Acts which are plainly mentioned in them, but the inward pleasing of our Hearts with such things as are forbidden, the Desires of our Hearts after them, or whatsoever is a probable means to give us that sinful Pleasure of our Thoughts, or further inflame such un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lawful Desires in our Souls.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">29 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ma<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. 1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.5<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> Mar 9.43<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                  </ns0:note> And if thy right eye <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>
                        <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 span">
                           <ns0:desc>〈…〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> to offe<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                           <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> offend thee, pluck it out, and cast <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> from thee, for it is profi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />table for thee that one of thy members should perish, and not that thy whole body should be cast into hell.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="30">30 And if thy right Hand offend thee, cut it off and cast <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> from thee, for it is profitable for thee that one of thy members should perish, and not that that thy whole body should be cast into hell.<ns0:note place="bottom">The sum of these two Verses is, That the Salvation of our immortal Souls, is to be preferred before all things, be they never so dear, and precious to us, and if that Mens ordinary Discretion teacheth them for the Preservation of their Bodies to cut off a particular Member, which would necessarily indanger the whole Body: It much more teacheth them to part with any thing, which will prejudice the Salvation of their Souls. Not that any Person is by this Text obliged to <ns0:hi>cut off any bodily Member</ns0:hi> (as some have done) because there can be no such ne<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cessity: but only to <ns0:hi>mortifie their Members, Col.</ns0:hi> 3.5. the <ns0:hi>Deeds</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>the Body, Rom.</ns0:hi> 8.13. <ns0:hi>their inward Lusts,</ns0:hi> which being <ns0:hi>mor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tified</ns0:hi> there will be no need of <ns0:hi>Mutilating</ns0:hi> our selves; for the <ns0:hi>Members of the Body,</ns0:hi> are but Commanded, and animated to their Motions, from the inward <ns0:hi>Lusts of the Heart</ns0:hi>: But if there could happen such a Case, as that a Man must <ns0:hi>voluntarily</ns0:hi> part with the most useful Member of his Body, or sin against God to the Damnation of his Soul, he ought rather to chuse the former than the latter. How much more then ought Christians to <ns0:hi>Mor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tifie</ns0:hi> their inward Lusts and unlawful Desires, which can be of no Profit nor Advantage to them: But will certainly make them to offend God, and so run them upon the Danger of Hell-fire?</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="31">31 It hath been said, whosoever <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Deut. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> Mat. 1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> Mar. 12 <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> shall put away his Wife, let him give her a writing of divorcement.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="32">32 But I say unto you, that <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luk. 16<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 1 Cor. 7.12.11.</ns0:note> whosoever shall put away his wife, saving for the cause of forni<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cation causeth her to commit adultery, and who<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />soever shall marry her that is divorced, committeth adultery.<ns0:note place="bottom">The Law to which our Saviour referreth here, or rather the <ns0:hi>Indulgence</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Toleration</ns0:hi> (for none was obliged to put away their <ns0:hi>Wives</ns0:hi> in Case of <ns0:hi>uncleanness</ns0:hi>) is that <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 24.1. where we have it in these words. <ns0:hi>When a Man hath taken a Wife and married her, and it cometh to pass, that she findeth no Favour in his Eyes, because he hath found some uncleanness in her, then let him write her a Bill of Divorcement and give it her in her hand, and send her out of his House.</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> had extended this <ns0:hi>Toleration</ns0:hi> which God gave Hus<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bands amongst the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> to other Cases, besides that of <ns0:hi>un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cleanness</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Adultery</ns0:hi>; so as they put away their Wives up<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on every <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>light occasion, interpreting those words [<ns0:hi>if she find no Favour in his Eyes</ns0:hi>] separately from the following words, <ns0:hi>because he hath found some uncleanness in her,</ns0:hi> and gave a Li<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />berty for Men upon any dislike of their Wives <ns0:hi>to put them away,</ns0:hi> provided that they first gave them a <ns0:hi>Bill of Divorcement,</ns0:hi> and that in these Cases it was lawful for the Parties thus sepa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rated each from other, to Marry to whom either of them pleased, and this is expressed in terms in their Form of those Writings of Divorcement, in <ns0:hi>Iosephus</ns0:hi> and other Writers. This indeed is a Case properly relating to the <ns0:hi>Iudicial Law,</ns0:hi> but all the <ns0:hi>Iudicial Laws</ns0:hi> are either <ns0:hi>Appendices</ns0:hi> to the <ns0:hi>Moral,</ns0:hi> or to the <ns0:hi>Ceremonial Law.</ns0:hi> This particular indulgence, was an <ns0:hi>Appendix</ns0:hi> to the <ns0:hi>Moral Law,</ns0:hi> by the seventh Com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mandment, to which our Saviour is now speaking, and giving the true Sense of it. He here opposeth the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> in two Points. 1. <ns0:hi>Asserting that all Divorces are unlawful except in cause of Adultery.</ns0:hi> 2. <ns0:hi>Asserting that whosoever Married her that was put away committed Adultery.</ns0:hi> It hath been a great Question, not so much amongst Divines as amongst Lawyers, <ns0:hi>Whether it be not lawful in any Case to put away a Wife, unless for Adultery</ns0:hi>? The <ns0:hi>Canonists</ns0:hi> have found out many Cases, in which they affirm it lawful. And the <ns0:hi>Coun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cel of Trent</ns0:hi> (from whom we may learn the Sense of the <ns0:hi>Po<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pish Divines) Anathematize</ns0:hi> those who deny the <ns0:hi>Church</ns0:hi> a Power of determining other Causes of <ns0:hi>Divorce.</ns0:hi> But their <ns0:hi>Blasphemous</ns0:hi> Curse falleth upon him, who is above them, <ns0:hi>God over all Blessed for ever,</ns0:hi> who in this Text hath determined that Point. Nor indeed did <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> give a <ns0:hi>Toleration</ns0:hi> in any other Cases. There may indeed be a parting betwixt <ns0:hi>Man</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Wife</ns0:hi> upon other Accounts: Either, <ns0:hi>wholly</ns0:hi> or in <ns0:hi>part.</ns0:hi> In Case one of them will part from the other, which the Apostle determineth, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 7.11.15. In which Case the Person de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />parting is only Guilty, if he or she Marry again. In Case of an Error, through <ns0:hi>ignorance</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>inadvertency</ns0:hi> upon the Marri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />age, that it appeareth, that the Persons married were such as by the <ns0:hi>Law of Nature,</ns0:hi> and of God ought not to have mar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ried, &c. But if we take <ns0:hi>Divorce</ns0:hi> for the <ns0:hi>voluntary Act of the Husband, putting away of his Wife:</ns0:hi> It is unlawful in any Case, but that of <ns0:hi>Adultery,</ns0:hi> which dissolves the Marriage knot and Covenant. 2. A second Question is also here deter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mined by our Saviour, <ns0:hi>viz. That it is unlawful for her, that is justly put away to Marry to any other, or for any other to Marry her wittingly.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="33">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:226" />33 Again, you have heard, that it hath been said by them of old time, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Deut. 5.11.</ns0:note> Thou shall not for<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />swear thy self, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Deut. 23.23.</ns0:note> but shall perform unto the Lord thy oaths.<ns0:note place="bottom">This was said, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 20.7. and more plainly, <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 19.12. the substance was there said, tho the words be not <ns0:hi>Verba<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tim</ns0:hi> recited.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="34">34 But I say unto you, Swear not all, neither by Heaven for it is <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Isa. 66.1.</ns0:note> Gods throne.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="35">35 Nor by the earth, for it is his Foot-stool, neither by Jerusalem, for it is <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 48.2.</ns0:note> the city of the great King.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="36">36 Neither shalt thou swear by thine head, because thou canst not make one hair white or black.<ns0:note place="bottom">Doth our Saviour here oppose himself to the Law of God, which saith <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 6.13.10.20. <ns0:hi>Thou shalt fear the Lord thy God,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>swear by his Name:</ns0:hi> Doth he condemn <ns0:hi>Abraham,</ns0:hi> who sware his Servant <ns0:hi>by the Lord God of Heaven and Earth, Gen.</ns0:hi> 24.3. doth he destroy such an <ns0:hi>useful mean,</ns0:hi> for the end of Strife, <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 6.16? None of all these: We must con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sider that our Saviour is here opposing himself to the Cor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ruptions of that Age brought in by the <ns0:hi>Pharisees,</ns0:hi> who had taught People that <ns0:hi>swearing</ns0:hi> was nothing, if they did not <ns0:hi>for<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />swear themselves,</ns0:hi> or at least <ns0:hi>swearing by the Heaven,</ns0:hi> by <ns0:hi>the Earth,</ns0:hi> by <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> by <ns0:hi>their Head,</ns0:hi> or in such like <ns0:hi>Forms</ns0:hi> was no sin, if they forbear the <ns0:hi>Name of God</ns0:hi>: That they were only obliged to swear by the Name of <ns0:hi>God</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>publick Courts of Iustice,</ns0:hi> but they were not tyed up to it at other times. To these and such like Corruptions our Saviour opposeth these words, I say unto you <ns0:hi>swear not all,</ns0:hi> not at all <ns0:hi>voluntarily,</ns0:hi> but where it is necessary for <ns0:hi>the end of Strife</ns0:hi>; not at all <ns0:hi>in your common Discourse, Ia.</ns0:hi> 5.12. and so it is expounded in the next Verse: The Law doth not only forbid <ns0:hi>false swearing,</ns0:hi> but <ns0:hi>common and ordinary swearing,</ns0:hi> needless <ns0:hi>swearing</ns0:hi> which speaks a great want of Reverence in the Heart, of the Name of God. And let not your Teachers cheat you, in telling you God, or the Name of God is not concerned, in your swearing <ns0:hi>by Hea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven.</ns0:hi> Is not Heaven the Throne of God? Or <ns0:hi>by Earth,</ns0:hi> is not that the <ns0:hi>Foot-stool of God</ns0:hi>? Or by <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> is not that <ns0:hi>the City of God.</ns0:hi> Or <ns0:hi>by your Head,</ns0:hi> is it not God that hath gi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven you your Life, and bodily Members? Is it in your Power to make <ns0:hi>an Hair of your Head, White or Black</ns0:hi>: So as the great thing here forbidden, is common and ordinary Swearing, where God calleth not us unto it, for the Determination of Strife. Do not only think that <ns0:hi>false Swearing,</ns0:hi> but be assured, that <ns0:hi>Ordinary, Common, needless Swearing</ns0:hi> is forbidden by God.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="37">37 But let your communication be Yea, Yea, Nay, Nay, for whatsoever <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> more than these cometh of evil.<ns0:note place="bottom">St. <ns0:hi>Iames</ns0:hi> saith much the same, <ns0:hi>Ia.</ns0:hi> 5.12. Let your ordina<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry Discourse in the World be meer Affirmations, or Denials of things in Terms, or <ns0:hi>Phrases</ns0:hi> of the same import, with <ns0:hi>Yea and Nay,</ns0:hi> tho you do not always use those Terms: Let <ns0:hi>Forms</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Swearing,</ns0:hi> be preserved for <ns0:hi>special times,</ns0:hi> when the Providence of God calls to you for them to determine strife, and make some weighty matters which you assert credible unto others who will not take your bare Assertions, have such a Reverence for the Name of God, as not to use it for every trifle, and let not my Ordinance for the <ns0:hi>end of Strife</ns0:hi> be made of no use, by your common use of the Name of God, for in ordinary Discourse, and common Talk, whatsoever is more than bare <ns0:hi>Affirmations</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Denials,</ns0:hi> cometh of an evil Heart or from the Devil, or from the Corruption of other mens Hearts. Some would make the <ns0:hi>Communication</ns0:hi> mentioned here, to be un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />derstood as if it were <ns0:hi>Conversation,</ns0:hi> or your ways of dealing with Men be plain without Fraud, and Guile, and so think our Saviour here strikes at the Root, and cause of so much idle and <ns0:hi>vain Swearing,</ns0:hi> viz. the common Falshood, Frauds, and Cosenages of Men in their dealings; but it seemeth hard so to interpret <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> in this place. Our Saviour especially being speaking concerning <ns0:hi>Words</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Forms of Speech.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="38">38 Ye have heard that it hath been said, An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth.<ns0:note place="bottom">This was the Commandement of God to the Magistrate, in Case a <ns0:hi>Woman with Child were struck, and any Mischief</ns0:hi> came of it, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 21.24. <ns0:hi>& Levit.</ns0:hi> 24.20. in <ns0:hi>C<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>se of Da<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mage done to a Neighbour,</ns0:hi> and in the Case of <ns0:hi>False-witness, Deut.</ns0:hi> 19.21. But in the mean time God had said to pri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vate Persons, <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 19.18. <ns0:hi>Thou shall not avenge,</ns0:hi> and it is said, <ns0:hi>Prov.</ns0:hi> 24.29. <ns0:hi>Say not, I will do to him, as he hath done to me.</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> had interpreted this Law of God, into a Liberty for every private Person, who had been wronged by another, to exact a Satisfaction upon him, provided that he did not exceed this Proportion of taking an <ns0:hi>Eye</ns0:hi> for an <ns0:hi>Eye,</ns0:hi> and a <ns0:hi>Tooth</ns0:hi> for a <ns0:hi>Tooth,</ns0:hi> doing no more wrong to another, than that other had done to him.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="39">39 But I say unto you, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Prov 24.29. Luk. 6.29. 1 Cor. 6.7. 1 Thes. 5.15. 1 Pet. 3.9.</ns0:note> That ye resist not evil, but whosoever shall smite thee on the right cheek, turn to him the other also.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="40">40 And if any man will sue thee at the law, and take away thy coat, let him have thy cloak also.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="41">41 And whosoever shall compel thee to go a mile, go with him twain.<ns0:note place="bottom">The Apostle <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> giveth the best Exposition upon this Text, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 12.17, 18, 19.21. <ns0:hi>Recompense to no man Evil for Evil—if it be possible as much as in you lyes, live Peaceably with all Men. Dearly beloved avenge not your selves, but rather give place unto Wrath,</ns0:hi> for it is written, <ns0:hi>Vengeance is mine, I will repay saith the Lord, v.</ns0:hi> 21. <ns0:hi>Be not overcome with Evil, but overcome Evil with Good,</ns0:hi> The general <ns0:hi>Scope</ns0:hi> of our <ns0:hi>Saviour</ns0:hi> is that which they must observe, who would understand the Sense of these words, they must not think that the particular things mentioned, are their Duty, but<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 1. That it is the Will of their Lord, that they should not take any private Revenge, but leave the avenging of their injuries unto God, and to the pub<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lick Magistrate, who is God's Vice-gerent, before whom not<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />withstanding any thing here said, they may seek a <ns0:hi>just Satis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />faction.</ns0:hi> 2. That in lighter Cases, we should rather remit the wrong done to us for Peace sake, than stand upon a Ri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gor of Justice, rather overcome Evil with Good, than suffer our selves to be overcome by the Evil of others. Rather suffer a blow on the other Cheek, than with our own Hands revenge the blow, which is given thus on our Cheek; rather loose our Cloak also, than contend for our Coat, taken away in Judgment from us, tho we be in that Judgment oppressed. No injury can deserve a private <ns0:hi>Revenge:</ns0:hi> Light injuries are not of that Nature, as we should contend for a publick Revenge of them.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="42">42 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luk. 6.30.</ns0:note> Give to him that asketh thee, and from him that would borrow of thee, turn thou not away.<ns0:note place="bottom">In these words our Saviour presseth another piece of <ns0:hi>Cha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rity,</ns0:hi> viz. <ns0:hi>Liberality</ns0:hi> to those who are <ns0:hi>Poor,</ns0:hi> who are of two sorts, some such as are never able to repay us, to those he Com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mandeth <ns0:hi>Christians</ns0:hi> to give, <ns0:hi>to him that asketh,</ns0:hi> who hath need to ask, and in that Order too which God hath directed, who hath Commanded us to <ns0:hi>provide for our own Houshold,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>to do Good to all, but especially to the Houshold of Faith.</ns0:hi> The other sort are such as may have only a <ns0:hi>Temporary want.</ns0:hi> To these he Commandeth us to <ns0:hi>lend,</ns0:hi> and not to <ns0:hi>turn away from them,</ns0:hi> when they desire to borrow of us, and we can spare it. This was an Ancient Precept of God, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 15.7, 8, 9. con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />firmed by Christ, as a piece of his Will under the Gospel.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
