Acts 7.60. 1 Pet. 2.23. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 3.9.</ns0:note> pray for them which despightfully use you, and persecute you.<ns0:note place="bottom">That this is no Counsel of <ns0:hi>Perfection</ns0:hi> (as the Papists would have it) nor any <ns0:hi>new Precept</ns0:hi> added to the Law of God (as the <ns0:hi>Socimans</ns0:hi> would have it) is plain from <ns0:hi>Prov.</ns0:hi> 25.21. where we find it commanded under the old Testament<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> Nei<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther is it I <ns0:hi>advise you,</ns0:hi> but <ns0:hi>I say unto you,</ns0:hi> which argueth a Command. <ns0:hi>Love</ns0:hi> here doth not signify the Complacency of the Heart in an object, which is Love in the strict Sense, but be <ns0:hi>Charitable unto, do good to</ns0:hi> your <ns0:hi>Enemies,</ns0:hi> nor are we equally obliged to do good to our <ns0:hi>Enemies</ns0:hi> as to our <ns0:hi>Friends,</ns0:hi> but it is Expounded by the following Words, and to be under<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>tood. 1. Of not seeking unlawful private Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />venge. <ns0:hi>Bless them that Curse you</ns0:hi>: do not return Reviling for Reviling, while they Curse, do you Bless. 2. Doing them common Offices of kindness. <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 12.20. <ns0:hi>If thine Enemy Hunger, feed him: if he Thirst, give him to Drink.</ns0:hi> This is a <ns0:hi>doing good</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>them that hate</ns0:hi> us, relieving them in their pre<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>sing Nece<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>sities 3. <ns0:hi>Doing them all the good we can for their Souls</ns0:hi>: Pray for them who Despightfully use you and Persecute you. So did our Saviour <ns0:hi>Lu.</ns0:hi> 23.43. and <ns0:hi>Stephen, Acts</ns0:hi> 7.60. so did <ns0:hi>David, Psal.</ns0:hi> 35.13, 14, 15. In the mean time we may hate those who are Gods Enemies, as such, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 139.21, 22. And for such, we may seek a due Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />venge of God's Honour upon them, and for our Enemies, this Precept Prohibits not the <ns0:hi>seeking of a just Satisfaction</ns0:hi> for Wrongs done unto us in a way of Publick Justice, yet not without a Mixture of Charity.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="45">45 That ye may be the children of your Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther which is in heaven, for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust.<ns0:note place="bottom">As your Heavenly Father, hath a <ns0:hi>common Love,</ns0:hi> which he extendeth to all Mankind, in supplying their Necessities, with the Light and Warmth of the Sun, and with the Rain as well as a <ns0:hi>special Love</ns0:hi> and Favour, which he exerciseth on<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly toward those that are good, and Members of Christ, so ought you to have, tho you are not obliged to take your <ns0:hi>Ene<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mies</ns0:hi> into your Bosom, yet you ought to <ns0:hi>love them</ns0:hi> in their order, and as your Heavenly Father, tho he will one Day have a Satisfaction from Sinners, for the wrong done to his Ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />jesty unless they Repent; yet to heap Coals of Fire on their Heads, gives them good things of <ns0:hi>Common Providence,</ns0:hi> that he might not leave them without Witness, yea, and affords them the <ns0:hi>outward means of Grace for their Souls</ns0:hi>: so al<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tho you are bound to seek some Satisfaction for Gods Ho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nour and Glory, from <ns0:hi>Flagitious Sinners,</ns0:hi> and tho you may in an orderly Course seek a moderate Satisfaction for the wrong done to your selves, yet you ought to love them, with a love consistent with these things. That so you may imitate your Heavenly Father, and approve your selves to <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>e his Children.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="46">
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Lu. 6.32.</ns0:note> 46 For if you love them that love you, what reward have you? do not even the publicans the same?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="47">47 And if you salute you brethren only, what do you more <ns0:hi>than others</ns0:hi>? do not even the publi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cans so?<ns0:note place="bottom">Reason obligeth you, who expect a reward from God for what you do, to do something more than those who know of no such reward; or at least live in no Expectation of any such thing, and you who Condemn others as great Sinners, and Men not worthy of your Converse, ought to do some<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thing by which you may outdo those whom you so Con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />de<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>n, both in Offices of <ns0:hi>Piety towards</ns0:hi> God, and <ns0:hi>Charity to<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />wards Men.</ns0:hi> But if you only shew kindness to your <ns0:hi>Relati<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ons,</ns0:hi> and to your <ns0:hi>Country-men,</ns0:hi> you do no more than those whom you look upon as Heathens, and the worst of Men, who act only from the Light and Law of Nature and know of no reward God hat<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> to give, nor live in any such Expecta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion of it. By <ns0:hi>loving</ns0:hi> here is me<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>nt doing <ns0:hi>good Offices,</ns0:hi> ei<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther for the <ns0:hi>Souls,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Bodies of others.</ns0:hi> By <ns0:hi>Saluting</ns0:hi> is meant Common Offices of kindness, such as inquiring of our Neigh<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bours Health, wishing the<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> well, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>Publicans</ns0:hi> were Civil Officers appointed by the Romans, to gather up Publick Taxes and Revenues, the Chief Commi<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>sioners were <ns0:hi>Knights</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Gentlemen</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Rome,</ns0:hi> who either let out these Revenues to others, or imployed others under them in the Collecting of them, these thus employed were some <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> (such were <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Zacheus</ns0:hi>) some <ns0:hi>Romans.</ns0:hi> These (as is ordina<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry) made their own Markets, and exacted of the People, upon which Accounts they were exceeding odious: and there<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore ordinarily in Scripture we shall find <ns0:hi>Publicans and Sin<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ners</ns0:hi> put together, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 9.11. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 11.19. and they are joyned with <ns0:hi>Harlots, Ch.</ns0:hi> 21.32. and the <ns0:hi>Pharisee</ns0:hi> in his Justificati<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on Gloried, he was not as <ns0:hi>that Publican, Lu.</ns0:hi> 18.11. Those who Condemn others, ought to take care that they be better than others.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="48">48 Be ye therefore perfect even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Perfect</ns0:hi> here is not taken in that Sense, as it is taken in other Texts of Scripture, where it signifyeth <ns0:hi>Sincerity</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>upright<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Iob</ns0:hi> 2.3. or where it signifieth a <ns0:hi>Comparative Per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fection,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> saith, he spake <ns0:hi>to those that were Perfect,</ns0:hi> but for an <ns0:hi>absolute perfecti<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>n,</ns0:hi> such as is in our <ns0:hi>Father which is in Heaven,</ns0:hi> and so much is signifyed by the proposing of our Heavenly Father as our <ns0:hi>Example.</ns0:hi> Nor will it therefore fol<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />low, either that thi<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> is a meer <ns0:hi>Counsel,</ns0:hi> not a <ns0:hi>Precept,</ns0:hi> or that an absolute <ns0:hi>Perfection</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>holiness,</ns0:hi> is a thing in this Life attain<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />able. But that it is our Duty to labour for it, <ns0:hi>forgetting what is behind,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>reaching forth unto those things which are before, pressing towards the Mark, for the Prize of the high Calling of God in Iesus Christ</ns0:hi> (as the <ns0:hi>Apostle</ns0:hi> speaks) <ns0:hi>Philip.</ns0:hi> 3.13, 14. <ns0:hi>Pro perfecto est, qui perfecto Proximus.</ns0:hi> God accounteth him Perfect, who is nearest to Perfection.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
